belief: The problem is that software and machines don't talk, and you have to own both to fix it.
scope_in: Manufacturing where the design-to-machine handoff is per-order and currently manual - every job needs its own geometry, toolpath, cost and schedule, and a person moves that information between CAD, CAM, ERP and the floor by hand. Excludes high-mix assembly with no per-order design step, and repeat job-shop reorders where engineering was done once and is re-run.
scope_industry: deliberately not fixed - selecting the wedge is this run's job
sisp_starting_solution: 'Vibe manufacturing' - a direct-to-consumer website where a customer specifies what they need and a factory the company owns makes it. Furniture as entry wedge advised by angel Daniel Theobald (Vecna Robotics) on the grounds that wood is easier to work than metal.
sisp_guard: Round 1 MUST use solution-free workflow language. No 'AI', 'automation', 'configurator', 'digital thread', 'vibe manufacturing', 'autonomous factory'. Establish whether the problem appears independently in how operators and buyers actually talk before any solution-shaped vocabulary is used.
hypotheses_not_filters: Furniture as the wedge (Theobald). The run may contradict it.
Direct-to-consumer as the channel. Testable, not a filter.
Owning the factory as required. Testable, not a filter.
H1 (fitted cabinetry via the trade channel) - retained as status: proposed, one candidate among others.
carried_evidence: E1-E6 from the prior desk-research pipeline, all graded 2/5 desk measurement. E1/E2: custom demand in freestanding furniture under 1% of generic, 14x thinner than cabinets. These are prior findings, NOT inputs the corpus should inherit - SISP probable requires independent establishment.
founder_request: Map the historical graveyard (Fab/Hem, Katerra, Made.com, Interior Define, Model No., Shapeways and peers) - routed to the required why-now-predecessor lens, widened from timing to full failure archaeology.
belief_disconfirmers: A company reaching batch-size-one economics on machines it does not own.
Interoperability standards (STEP AP242, MTConnect, UMATI, QIF) closing the gap without anyone owning both ends.
